question: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is the statutory body responsible for regulating food safety standards in India, replacing the older Prevention of Food Adulteration (PFA) Act.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. FSSAI was established under the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 and replaced the Prevention of Food Adulteration (PFA) Act 1954. It is now the single apex regulatory body for food safety in India.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 established FSSAI, which subsumed the PFA Act 1954 along with several other food-related laws. FSSAI sets standards, licenses food businesses, and conducts surveillance sampling.
